To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the competitive mode preferences and the satisfaction towards a learning experience are different for different students.

(1) students' preferences towards computerized competition modes differ; (2) students' satisfaction towards the learning process differs depending on the competition modes; (3) anonymity has a positive influence on the students' emotional states; (4) the students' emotional state has a positive influence in the students' satisfaction with the learning process.
students' learning preferences and their satisfaction towards the learning process are affected by the mode of competition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, development and implementation of computerized competitive modes in an online drill-and-practice system.
the design and development, as well as the evaluation of the effectiveness of a computerized competitive learning system.
the design and evaluation of a competitive learning environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
competitive learning systems are a promising and useful learning tool for students.
competitive gaming systems are a valuable addition to the e-learning environment.
a competitive learning system is an effective and efficient learning tool which should be incorporated into the learning process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the design of competitive learning environments is a promising direction for e-learning research.
the design and development process of the competitive gaming system JOYCE was a success.
the competitive gaming system is a promising approach to engage students in learning activities.
The main takeaway from our work is that

competition in a learning context can be a powerful motivator for learning and that it is important to understand the different competition modes and the different learning mode preferences to design and implement effective e-learning systems.
competition can be used as a tool to increase students' motivation to learn, but it is not always a positive experience.
the design of competitive e-learning environments should be based on the learning mode preferences of the users and the learning objectives of the course.
